sentences.text: Dr.Khuzema Kapadia - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Tarun Pagare -Ga appearing on behalf of Advocate Ge
 Shri Vinay Joshi, Advocate for the respondent/objector.

Order 
1] They are heard and perused the case diary.

2] This is the applicant's first bail application filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.27/2024 registered at Police Station Crime Branch District- Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 137(2), 64(1), 64(2)M, 65(1), 87, 127(4) of B.N.S., 2023 09,420,467,468 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Crime Branch District- Indore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 12/1/2025.

3] The allegation against the applicant is of committing fraud to the tune of Rs.9,75,000/- as the complainant was duped by the applicant on the pretext of providing travel services which included booking tickets, travelling visa, hotels and flight booking for Dubai.
It is alleged that after obtaining the aforesaid amount the applicant neither provided the services as assured nor returned the amount to the complainant.

4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case,
as the amount which was received by the applicant in different accounts was actually for the purposes of providing services only, as the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant has been in jail since 12/1/2025 and the final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.

5] Counsel for the respondent/State as also counsel for the objector, have opposed the prayer, and it is submitted that no case for interference is made out as the applicant has committed two similar offences in the State of Chhattisgarh, two cases in the State of Jharkhand and one in the State of Uttar Pradesh.

Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case- diary and the fact that five similar cases have also been registered against the applicant in three difference States, it clearly demonstrates that the applicant has the propensity to commit the same offence again and again, and in such circumstances, when he has also not shown an inclination to remit the amount to the complainant, this Court does not finds it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
